summary: Anthony Tribe is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford in 1995 under Alexis Sanderson, having also studied under Paul Williams and Steven Collins. He held posts at the University of Montana (attested 1997) and the University of Arizona (attested 2020).

Antoine Cabaton (1863–1942) worked in linguistics, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École du Louvre and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1895–1899), and served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1900–1920).
Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco J. Varela.

Antoine Meillet (1866–1936) was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Paris/Sorbonne and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, James Darmesteter, and Ferdinand de Saussure. He taught at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1758–1838) worked in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He held chairs at INALCO and the Collège de France (1806–1838), founded and presided over the Société Asiatique, and served as perpetual secretary of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier (1741–1795) was an Indologist and historian. He studied under traditional teacher Ramchandra and served as a colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy (1773–1832) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, taught Persian at INALCO, and held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

Anton Boller (1811–1869) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served at the University of Vienna as Dozent, extraordinary professor (from 1850), and professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit from 1855, and was a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca (1810–1884) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned his Dr. phil. at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831), where he later lectured (1849–1852), and also held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

Anton Schiefner (1817–1879) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University (1836–1840) and Oriental studies at Humboldt University of Berlin (1840–1842). His posts included the Russian Academy of Sciences and Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy.
Anton Westermann (1806–1869) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

Antonino Forte (1940–2006) specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hōbōgirin (~1976–1986), the Italian School of East Asian Studies/Kyoto Center (~1982–1996), École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1986), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1987–2006).

Antonio T. de Nicolás (1930–2022) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Fordham University and served at Stony Brook University (~1969–1996) as professor emeritus of philosophy.

Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (2010) under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, also studying under Ramon N. Prats and traditional teachers. He is a scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Anuj Misra works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, and held an external researcher post at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he served as assistant lecturer in Pali (attested 1943), studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, and later served as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Monier Monier-Williams (~1864–1866) and served at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), Presidency University (~1878–1895), and as principal of Aliah University (~1878–1895).
Arghyadip Mondal works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. As of 2026, he is attested as a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Arindam Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford and held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1999), the University of Hawaiʻi (attested 2009–2026, now emeritus), and Stony Brook University (attested 2026).
